boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Documented Tufts rituals, landmarks, music, and annual gatherings—plus one clearly marked historical custom.

cards.title: Paint the Cannon
cards.subtitle: Cannon beside Goddard Chapel
cards.notes: Plan a message for the cannon only, paint after dark, and follow Tufts’ current guidance on respectful, non-offensive expression.
cards.short_summary: A student-painted campus landmark used for announcements, commemoration, and expression.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts says students have painted the Cannon since 1977, generally after dark, to commemorate moments, promote groups, or for fun.
cards.access_notes: Follow university painting guidance; do not paint adjacent trees, walkways, or other surfaces.

cards.title: Mark Tufts’ Birthday at Tuftonia’s Day
cards.subtitle: Annual end-of-spring-semester carnival
cards.notes: Look for the annual campus carnival near the end of spring semester; the official tradition page identifies games, rides, and food trucks.
cards.short_summary: Tufts’ annual birthday celebration arrives just before final-exam season.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts describes Tuftonia’s Day as an annual celebration of the university’s birthday that marks the end of the spring semester.
cards.access_notes: Event details and participation arrangements vary by year.

cards.title: Pass the Light at Illumination
cards.subtitle: President’s Lawn beneath Goddard Chapel
cards.notes: New students and graduates can join this candle-lighting ritual at its scheduled orientation or Commencement-week gathering on the President’s Lawn.
cards.short_summary: A candle-lit bookend to the Tufts student experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts calls Illumination a longstanding tradition held during new-student Orientation and again on the eve of Commencement.
cards.access_notes: The 2026 incoming-student ceremony is scheduled for September 3; check the Chaplaincy page for current details.

cards.title: Hear “Tuftonia’s Day”
cards.subtitle: Tufts football games, Homecoming, and a cappella concerts
cards.notes: Listen for the 1912 fight song at a football game, especially Homecoming, or at a Tufts a cappella concert.
cards.short_summary: The school song connects athletics, Homecoming, and campus vocal groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts says “Tuftonia’s Day,” written in 1912 by alumnus Elliot W. Hayes, is performed at most football games and especially at Homecoming.
cards.access_notes: Check athletics and performing-arts calendars for scheduled public events.

cards.title: Know Jumbo’s Exam-Season Lore
cards.subtitle: Jumbo the Elephant and the former Barnum Hall display
cards.notes: See the Jumbo statue and learn the old exam-season ritual: students once tugged Jumbo’s tail and set a penny on his trunk.
cards.short_summary: A mascot-centered luck custom preserved in Tufts’ institutional history.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts records that students tugged Jumbo’s tail and placed a penny on his trunk for good luck during exam season.
cards.access_notes: This describes historical mascot lore; do not handle or alter campus objects.

cards.title: Gather for Spring Fling
cards.subtitle: Academic Quad before final exams
cards.notes: Watch for the annual pre-finals concert on the Academic Quad, and use the official event announcements for lineup and entry details.
cards.short_summary: Since 1980, a campus concert has provided a collective pause before finals.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts says students have gathered on the Academic Quad for the Spring Fling concert immediately before finals since 1980.
cards.access_notes: Lineup, access, and event rules vary by year.

cards.title: Spot the Res Quad’s Reservoir Legend
cards.subtitle: Res Quad, named for the former reservoir
cards.notes: Walk through the Res Quad and read its lore as a historical campus legend; its “unbreakable date” claim is not a rule or promise.
cards.short_summary: A former water-supply site left behind an enduring, tongue-in-cheek courtship legend.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts says the Res Quad’s name refers to a former reservoir and records a tradition that dates made there could not be broken.
cards.access_notes: Treat this as campus folklore, not an expectation or obligation.

cards.title: Read the Bowen Gate Legend
cards.subtitle: Bowen Gate on the Medford/Somerville campus
cards.notes: Pause at Bowen Gate for its campus story; the supposed marriage outcome after a kiss is a legend, not a prediction.
cards.short_summary: A named campus gate carries a lighthearted piece of Tufts courtship folklore.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts records the legend that kissing someone under Bowen Gate means the pair will someday marry.
cards.access_notes: Respect consent and treat the claim as folklore.

cards.title: Carry the Tradition to the Pops
cards.subtitle: Alumni Weekend in Boston
cards.notes: If you are eligible for Alumni Weekend, check the current program for Tufts Night at the Pops, an event the archives trace to 1901.
cards.short_summary: An Alumni Weekend concert tradition with more than a century of documented history.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts’ Commencement exhibition identifies Tufts Night at the Pops as a long-standing Alumni Weekend tradition dating to 1901.
cards.source_title: Alumni Weekend | A Step into the Unknown
cards.access_notes: Availability, tickets, and eligibility are set by the current Alumni Weekend program.

cards.title: Remember the Freshman Beanies
cards.subtitle: Historical Tufts custom, discontinued in 1969
cards.notes: Browse Tufts’ historical account and photographs of freshman beanies, a campus custom that began in 1854 and ended in 1969.
cards.short_summary: A long-running first-year identifier now preserved as campus history rather than a current practice.
cards.evidence_claim: Tufts Now reports that freshman beanies were a Tufts tradition from 1854 until the practice ended in 1969.
cards.access_notes: Discontinued historical tradition; view it through Tufts archival materials rather than attempting to recreate it.
